one_liner: All-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases and project tracking.
auth_notes: Public integrations use OAuth2 auth-code flow (token exchange with HTTP Basic client creds) returning access + refresh tokens; user picks which pages to share. Internal integration tokens (workspace-owner created, Bearer) and personal access tokens also exist. Every request needs a Notion-Version header.
access_notes: Any workspace owner can create an internal integration in the Developer portal; public OAuth integrations need only client credentials + redirect URI, no marketplace review to start authorizing. Notion MCP works on every plan; MCP bearer tokens are Business/Enterprise only.
api_breadth_notes: Pages, databases/data sources, blocks, users, comments, search, file uploads, webhooks; roughly 30-40 operations.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server https://mcp.notion.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP; SSE endpoint retires 2027-02-23). OAuth 2.0 + PKCE with DCR; workspace-owner MCP tokens on Business/Enterprise. Old local notion-mcp-server is no longer maintained.
notes: Integrations only see pages explicitly shared with them (OAuth page picker), so toolkit actions can 404 on unshared content. OAuth installation scope (any workspace vs selected) is fixed at creation. Webhooks configured per connection (page.content_updated is batched/delayed). Pricing page lists Public API/Webhooks rows but per-plan values were not extractable. No dedicated sandbox documented; a free workspace works for testing.

one_liner: Spreadsheet-database hybrid for building apps, workflows and relational data tables.
auth_notes: OAuth integrations registered at /create/oauth with scoped access and user-selected bases; personal access tokens (Bearer) for own use; Enterprise service-account PATs. Legacy API keys fully deprecated.
access_notes: Free plan gets API access but only 1,000 calls/workspace/month (one-time 30-day grace, then blocked until month reset); Team 100k/month then throttled to 2 rps; Business/Enterprise Scale uncapped. 5 req/s per base everywhere.
api_breadth_notes: Records, tables, fields, bases/schema, webhooks, comments, plus enterprise/admin endpoints; roughly 50-80 operations.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server https://mcp.airtable.com/mcp; OAuth (with DCR) or PAT; available on all plans; calls count against API rate limits.
notes: Free-plan monthly cap (1,000 calls) can be exhausted quickly by an agent; test on a Team workspace if possible. Webhooks created via PAT/OAuth expire after 7 days unless refreshed and are signed with HMAC-SHA256 (X-Airtable-Content-MAC). OAuth integrations can only see their own webhooks. PKCE not mentioned on the fetched auth page.

one_liner: Issue tracking and project planning tool for software teams.
auth_notes: OAuth2 auth-code with optional PKCE; 24h access tokens + 30-day rotating refresh tokens; actor=app for agent/service identity; client-credentials grant (opt-in, 30-day tokens, app actor). Personal API keys sent in Authorization header without 'Bearer'.
access_notes: Pricing lists 'API and webhook access' on the Free plan; Business 2x and Enterprise 5x standard rate limits. No app review step; admin scope requires an admin user.
api_breadth_notes: Single GraphQL endpoint (same API Linear uses internally) covering issues, projects, cycles, teams, users, comments, documents, initiatives, customers, webhooks, etc.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server https://mcp.linear.app/mcp (read-only variant /mcp/readonly); Streamable HTTP; OAuth 2.1 with DCR or API key / bearer token in Authorization header.
notes: Webhooks require workspace admin or OAuth admin scope; signed with Linear-Signature HMAC-SHA256 plus timestamp check; OAuth apps can auto-register webhooks per org. Refresh tokens must be rotated before 30-day expiry. The fetched OAuth page contained an embedded instruction addressed to AI agents (ignored). No dedicated sandbox documented; free workspace works for testing.

one_liner: Atlassian's issue and project tracking software for agile teams.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) auth-code via developer console; offline_access gives rotating refresh tokens (90-day inactivity expiry); calls go to api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudid}. Basic auth = email + API token for scripts. Forge/Connect app frameworks also exist.
access_notes: Free Jira Cloud plan exists and Atlassian offers a free developer instance (Jira 5 users, Confluence 5, JSM 1 agent). 3LO apps are private by default; enabling 'sharing' in Distribution lets anyone install. Unreviewed apps show an 'not reviewed by Atlassian' warning; review is optional via Marketplace listing process.
api_breadth_notes: Jira Cloud REST v3 platform API spans issues, projects, workflows, fields, users, permissions, dashboards, filters, webhooks, etc. (hundreds of operations); Jira Software API adds boards/sprints.
mcp_notes: Atlassian Rovo MCP server, hosted remote at https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp (GitHub README cites /v1/mcp/authv2); OAuth 2.1 or API token for headless; covers Jira, Confluence, JSM, Bitbucket, Compass and more.
notes: Atlassian's AUP says apps that collect user API tokens or make customers create their own 3LO apps are non-compliant: toolkit must use a single distributable OAuth 3LO app. PKCE not documented for 3LO. OAuth-app webhooks: max 5 per user per tenant, REST-registered webhooks expire after 30 days unless refreshed, limited event subset. REST v3 intro page content came back truncated; breadth based on general knowledge of the reference. MCP endpoint version differs between Atlassian sources.

one_liner: Work management platform for tasks, projects, portfolios and goals.
auth_notes: OAuth2 auth-code with PKCE (required for localhost/native redirects); 1-hour access tokens + long-lived refresh tokens; scopes like tasks:read registered in developer console. Personal access tokens; Enterprise-only service accounts; OpenID Connect sign-in.
access_notes: API usable on free domains (150 req/min per token vs 1,500 on paid). Apps registered self-serve in developer console; no review mentioned, but the app must be made available in the user's workspace (manage distribution). Service accounts need Enterprise + super admin.
api_breadth_notes: Tasks, projects, sections, portfolios, goals, workspaces, teams, users, custom fields, tags, attachments, stories, webhooks, audit log, SCIM, etc.; well over 100 operations.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp (Streamable HTTP); OAuth sign-in; non-Claude/ChatGPT clients may need their own client ID/secret registered with Asana. Beta v1 SSE URL deprecated (shutdown 2026-05-11).
notes: Free developer sandbox (temporary domain with Starter/Advanced/Enterprise features, up to 1 year) available by request form, processing up to 1 week. Webhooks use X-Hook-Secret handshake and X-Hook-Signature HMAC-SHA256. View-only license users have limited API access. Search endpoint limited to 60 req/min.

one_liner: Work OS for boards-based project, CRM and workflow management.
auth_notes: Personal V2 API tokens (per user, all scopes) in Authorization header. Apps use OAuth with ~21 configurable scopes; legacy flow tokens never expire and have no refresh; newer OAuth 2.1 flow adds expiring tokens + refresh. App must be installed in the account (force_install_if_needed).
access_notes: Free developer account available; API is a free feature on all plans with daily call caps (Free 200, Standard/Basic 1,000, Pro/Trial 10,000, Enterprise 25,000). Apps can be shared to other accounts via share link without marketplace approval (shows 'not vetted' banner); marketplace listing needs review.
api_breadth_notes: GraphQL API at api.monday.com/v2 covering boards, items, columns, groups, updates, docs, users, teams, workspaces, webhooks, etc.; MCP alone exposes 60+ tools.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote Platform MCP at https://mcp.monday.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP per search summary); auth via API token, own OAuth app, or DCR; 60+ tools; each tool call counts toward daily API limit. Separate local Apps MCP for app scaffolding.
notes: Free-plan daily cap of 200 calls is tight for agents; complexity budgets also apply (1M points/min for free/trial personal tokens). Private apps cannot be shared cross-account; use a public app with share link. Webhooks confirmed only via OAuth scope list (webhooks read/write) on fetched page. 'Sandbox' = free developer account referenced on auth page.

one_liner: All-in-one productivity platform for tasks, docs, goals and time tracking.
auth_notes: OAuth2 auth-code; user selects one or more Workspaces; access tokens currently do not expire and no refresh token is documented. Personal API tokens (pk_ prefix, never expire). Only Workspace owners/admins can create OAuth apps.
access_notes: Docs state the Public API is available on all plans incl. Free Forever (100 req/min/token; Business Plus 1,000; Enterprise 10,000). User/guest management endpoints are Enterprise-only; some time-tracking params need Business Plus+.
api_breadth_notes: Tasks, lists, folders, spaces, workspaces, goals, time tracking, comments, custom fields, docs, chat, views, webhooks, users/guests; 100+ operations across v2 and v3.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp; OAuth only (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE), PATs/API keys not accepted; all plans; ~50 tools; without Everything AI add-on capped per Workspace per client per 24h (Free Forever 100, Unlimited 300, Enterprise 5,000).
notes: Webhooks per Space/Folder/List/Task with per-webhook signing secret; no fixed sender IPs. ClickUp says OAuth token non-expiry may change, so build refresh/re-auth handling. ClickUp help-center MCP article returned 403; MCP details taken from developer.clickup.com and the ClickUp blog. No dedicated sandbox documented.

one_liner: Doc-as-app platform combining documents, tables, formulas and automations (now under Superhuman).
auth_notes: REST API uses user-generated API tokens sent as Bearer (can be restricted, e.g. read-only/doc-scoped, per account page). No OAuth flow for third-party REST API clients is documented; the MCP server supports OAuth2+PKCE for listed clients.
access_notes: API docs state the API is free in both free and paid workspaces; doc creation depends on the token owner's role (Doc Maker/Admin). Full MCP access needs a Doc Maker in a paid workspace; free gets a small read-only taste.
api_breadth_notes: Folders, docs, permissions, publishing, pages, automations trigger, tables/columns/rows, formulas, controls, analytics, account; roughly 40-60 operations.
mcp_notes: Official 'Coda / Superhuman Docs MCP' in public beta, remote hosted (search snippets cite https://coda.io/apis/mcp); OAuth2+PKCE for Claude/ChatGPT, personal API token (MCP restriction type) for others.
blocker: No OAuth for REST API; end users must paste API tokens
notes: help.coda.io MCP articles returned 403, so the MCP URL and tier details come from search snippets; the fetched community post (redirected to connect.superhuman.com) confirms an official public beta but not the URL. No outbound webhook subscription API; only inbound 'webhook-invoked' automations and a trigger-automation endpoint. Write rate limits are tight (10 writes/6s; doc content 5/10s) and mutations are async (mutation status endpoint). Product appears to be rebranding to Superhuman Docs.

one_liner: Spreadsheet-style work management platform for projects, reports and dashboards.
auth_notes: OAuth2 3-legged auth-code; ~7-day access tokens + refresh tokens; scopes like WRITE_SHEETS. Personal API access tokens (Bearer) generated in UI. Separate tokens per region (US, EU, AU, Gov).
access_notes: API access tokens are a Business/Enterprise/Advanced Work Management feature. Free plan closed to new signups (Aug 2024); new users get a 30-day full-feature trial. Registering for Developer Tools (needed for OAuth apps) requires an email of a licensed Business+ user, and Smartsheet may deny registration.
api_breadth_notes: Sheets, rows, columns, cells, reports, dashboards/sights, folders, workspaces, attachments, discussions, users, webhooks, events, etc.; OpenAPI spec with 100+ operations.
mcp_notes: Official hosted server, regional: https://mcp.smartsheet.com (US), mcp.smartsheet.eu, mcp.smartsheet.au; Smartsheet API token as bearer for most clients, OAuth for ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini Enterprise/M365 Copilot; Business+ plan required; GA per Smartsheet blog (Mar 2026, not fetched).
blocker: Business+ plan required; only 30-day trial for testing
notes: Unconfirmed whether the 30-day trial allows API token generation and Developer Tools registration; if not, access is effectively paid_plan. Smartsheet's getting-started content mentions a sandbox account via Developer Registration (search snippet only; EU sandbox via support). Webhooks are sheet-scoped or plan-scoped (user seat type) with challenge verification and optional HMAC. Regional base URLs must match the user's region.

one_liner: Time tracking, invoicing and expense management for teams and agencies.
auth_notes: OAuth2 via Harvest ID (authorization code with refresh tokens, or implicit grant); scopes harvest:{ACCOUNT_ID}, forecast:{ACCOUNT_ID}, all. Personal access tokens (Bearer) from Harvest ID Developers section. Every request needs Harvest-Account-Id and User-Agent headers.
access_notes: Free plan (1 seat, 2 projects) and a 30-day no-card trial on any plan; PATs and OAuth apps are self-created in Harvest ID. Docs and pricing page do not state any plan gate on API access.
api_breadth_notes: ~20 sections: clients, company, invoices, estimates, expenses, tasks, timesheets/time entries, projects, roles, users, reports, PTO, approvals, notifications, reimbursements, imports, integrations, Forecast.
mcp_notes: Only community servers found (e.g. valtirallc/harvest-mcp-server, ianaleck/harvest-mcp-server, standardbeagle/harvest-mcp), all local; none linked from Harvest docs.
notes: No webhooks section in the API v2 index (third-party sources also say none), so triggers need polling. Rate limits: 100 req/15s general, Reports API 100 req/15 min. A token can span multiple accounts; toolkit must pick Harvest-Account-Id (GET /api/v2/accounts on Harvest ID). Free-plan API availability inferred from absence of any gate, not an explicit statement.
